provenance.resolutionNote: Decree 05-468, read in full while specifically searching for 'avoir'/'rectif'/'correct' by the issue #558 research pass (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md, section 4), nowhere defines a 'facture d'avoir' (credit note): discounts and rebates are folded into the original invoice at the moment it is created (art. 5-6), never corrected afterwards through a separate document. The native contributor for issue #558, asked directly whether a credit note or equivalent exists in practice, answered on 2026-09-30: "I'm not sure but in practice yes, there should be a credit note": itself an uncertain answer, not a confident practice claim. What would settle it: the Systeme Comptable Financier or the CTCA's own VAT-regularization rules (art. 78 equivalent), neither reached by this research pass.

routes.notes: Source: issue #558, native contributor, 2026-09-30 (uncertain practice answer) plus a full, negative reading of decree 05-468.

provenance.resolutionNote: Same full reading of decree 05-468 as CREDIT_NOTE above: no upward-correction document is defined either. The native contributor was not asked specifically about a debit note (only about a credit note / 'facture d'avoir' generally). What would settle it: the same Systeme Comptable Financier / CTCA regularization provisions named for CREDIT_NOTE above.

routes.notes: Decree 05-468, read in full, silent on this route: not researched further.

provenance.resolutionNote: Decree 05-468 defines no general rectifying-document mechanism distinct from the cancellation mechanism read for CANCEL_AND_REPLACE below (art. 10's own 'facture annulee' mention). No provision naming a document that amends an already-issued invoice BY REFERENCE, without being a credit or debit note, was identified. What would settle it: the same Systeme Comptable Financier / CTCA texts named for CREDIT_NOTE above, read specifically for this mechanism.

routes.notes: Not identified by a full reading of decree 05-468 (issue #558 research pass, RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md section 4).

provenance.resolutionNote: Decree 05-468 art. 10, last sentence, read in full and quoted verbatim by the issue #558 research pass: "La facture regulierement annulee doit faire l'objet d'une mention << facture annulee >> inscrite clairement en diagonale." This describes a real cancellation mechanism, but it does NOT match this route's own definition: the mention is written ON THE ORIGINAL document itself, which is kept in the carnet a souches (the invoice booklet): there is no reissuance under a NEW number described anywhere in the text, which is what CANCEL_AND_REPLACE presupposes. The research pass explicitly flagged this mismatch rather than forcing a fit. For a simple material error, the text is silent and even forbids erasure (art. 10's own 'ne comprendre aucune tache, rature ou surcharge'): by deduction (not a sentence of the text) a faulty invoice is probably cancelled this way and then reissued at the NEXT number, which is closer to this route's shape than to any exact match, but that reissuance-at-the-next-number step is inferred, not read. What would settle it: DGI doctrine or a provision explicitly describing reissuance under a new number after a cancellation.

routes.notes: Decree 05-468 art. 10 (verbatim quote above) describes a real, but imperfectly matching, cancellation mechanism.

provenance.resolutionNote: No credit-note mechanism at all was identified for Algeria (see CREDIT_NOTE above), so a purely internal variant of one could not be checked either. What would settle it: the same texts named for CREDIT_NOTE above, once a credit-note mechanism itself is identified.

routes.notes: Not reachable before CREDIT_NOTE itself is settled.

provenance.resolutionNote: Decree 05-468's own cancellation mechanism (art. 10, see CANCEL_AND_REPLACE above) is an act of the ISSUER itself (the seller writes 'facture annulee' on the original): nothing in the text describes a cancellation DECIDED or carried out by the tax authority, at the issuer's request or of its own motion. Algeria has no real-time invoice clearance platform (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md section 5: no e-invoicing or telereporting obligation found in any of the seven finance laws, three consolidated tax codes, or the DGI's own site, read or searched), which is the usual context an authority-side annulment mechanism exists in elsewhere in this catalog. What would settle it: DGI doctrine confirming the absence (or existence) of an authority-initiated cancellation power over an already-issued invoice.

routes.notes: No authority-side mechanism identified; the one cancellation mechanism found (decree 05-468 art. 10) is issuer-initiated.

provenance.resolutionNote: This route presupposes a rejection scenario by a clearance platform: a scenario that does not exist for Algeria (see AUTHORITY_ANNULMENT above: no e-invoicing or clearance platform found by the issue #558 research pass). No mechanism for reissuing an invoice under the SAME date and number after any kind of rejection was identified. What would settle it: the same DGI doctrine named for AUTHORITY_ANNULMENT above.

routes.notes: Not applicable absent a clearance platform, on the evidence gathered so far; not positively excluded.

provenance.resolutionNote: No mechanism for reissuing an invoice under the SAME number with an added note, for a correction with no tax effect, was identified in decree 05-468. The closest finding, art. 10's own cancellation mention (see CANCEL_AND_REPLACE above), annotates the ORIGINAL document itself rather than producing a duplicate, and concerns a full cancellation, not a no-tax-effect correction. What would settle it: DGI doctrine or a provision describing a same-number reissuance mechanism for a correction that does not affect the tax computation.

routes.notes: Decree 05-468 art. 10's cancellation mention is the closest finding but does not match this route's own definition.

provenance.resolutionNote: No provision governing a correction made only in the accounting register or a VAT return, without any document at all reaching the customer, was identified: the issue #558 research pass did not reach the CTCA's own VAT-regularization articles (the equivalent of Portugal's CIVA art. 78, for instance) or the Systeme Comptable Financier. What would settle it: those two texts, read directly for this specific mechanism.

routes.notes: Not reached by the issue #558 research pass (RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md's own 'Ce que je n'ai pas pu verifier' section).

provenance.resolutionNote: No scenario was identified where a correction would take effect automatically, by operation of law alone, with no document and no accounting entry required at all. Nothing read by the issue #558 research pass (decree 05-468 in full) describes such a mechanism. What would settle it: the same CTCA/Systeme Comptable Financier texts named for LEDGER_ANNOTATION above.

routes.notes: Not identified; not reached in enough depth to positively exclude either.

provenance.resolutionNote: No mechanism allowing the RECIPIENT of an Algerian invoice to unilaterally reject it, with the effect of making it lose its status as an invoice, was identified in decree 05-468 (read in full by the issue #558 research pass). What would settle it: the CTCA's own VAT-deduction provisions and general commercial-law texts on the recipient's own obligations, neither reached by this research pass for this specific question.

routes.notes: Not identified by a full reading of decree 05-468.

notes: Algeria (DZ), issue #558, transcribed 2026-09-30 from RECHERCHE_558_ALGERIE.md (section 4) plus the native contributor's own answers on issue #558 (2026-09-30). Decree executif n. 05-468 du 10 decembre 2005 (JO n. 80 du 11 decembre 2005) was read IN FULL while specifically searching for a correction/cancellation mechanism: it defines exactly one, an issuer-written 'facture annulee' mention in diagonal on the original document (art. 10, quoted verbatim in the CANCEL_AND_REPLACE route above), and is otherwise silent on every one of the eleven canonical routes this catalog covers. All eleven routes are therefore honestly 'unverified' rather than forced onto a route the text does not cleanly describe: the research pass itself explicitly declined to stretch the one mechanism it found (CANCEL_AND_REPLACE's own definition presupposes a reissuance under a new number, which the text does not describe) into a false 'legal' match. No e-invoicing or clearance platform was found for Algeria (section 5 of the same research pass), which rules out several routes' usual context (AUTHORITY_ANNULMENT, RESUBMIT_SAME_IDENTITY) without ruling out the routes themselves. Comparable, per that research pass's own estimate, to where Portugal's own correction-routes file stood after its first pass (four of eleven sourced 'legal'): Algeria's own first pass sources zero of eleven as 'legal', a materially thinner result the PR report names plainly rather than smoothing over.
